context: Packaged-image serving (deepseek-v41-flash-sm120:latest), TP8/EP8 flashinfer_mxfp4, DSpark block 3, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PHB, PCIe PHB topology without NVLink.
motivation: Live torch-profiler traces attributed 53% (decode C32) and 55% (32k prefill) of GPU busy time to ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16_RING_LL. Standalone microbenchmarks showed the NCCL tuner picking LL at ~1.3MB where Simple is ~1.7x faster.
protocol: 3 rounds per leg, medians; 768-output-token greedy requests, ignore_eos, cache flushed per cell; C4/C16 legs ran after the C1/C32 legs, one server restart apart.

custom_p2p_allreduce_rejected.method: NVLink policy gate bypassed experimentally in a disposable container; numerics verified (rel err ~4e-3 vs NCCL, bf16 reduction order)
custom_p2p_allreduce_rejected.conclusion: One-shot/two-shot P2P kernels are 15-30x slower than NCCL over PCIe host bridges; upstream NVLink gate is correct for this topology.

decision: Kit default keeps the NCCL protocol tuner (NCCL_PROTO empty). Simple is a documented opt-in for saturated-batch serving only.
caveats: Topology-specific (PCIe PHB, no NVLink); not transferable to NVLink hosts.
NCCL_PROTO applies per process; no per-message-size override exists.
Aggregate rates are batch output sums over wall time, not per-request decode rates.
